title: Revenge is costly; the music marketplace; Capitol money withheld
summary: Gil says revenge is too costly and describes waiting on money from Capitol held by a lawyer.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Managers, bookers and the business of getting work

blocks.x: In a way it's a waste of time to, what do you call it, to overbeat it, you know what I mean. Like once the horse is dead there is no use beating it. So a lot of it, while still alive and you can make people squirm and move over for you and give you some opportunity, it works fine. When it becomes just a

thing like a chronic, a chronic effort at revenge which isn't going to cost you too much, then you're in trouble. Because even though it is sweet is very expensive. It doesn't make any difference who or where, revenge unless it comes unexpectedly, or as a bargain, there's no such thing as a bargain that doesn't just happens.

You try to make a bargain, it never works. And revenge is something that really is too costly. I have to tell myself that all the time. Because there are people just waiting around for you to kill them you know, to get even with you. (LAUGHTER). They really are, you know, really. Yes, yes.
So that you will get punished for doing it, yes, yes.

Oh that's right. I know people like that in the business, booking agents and all those sleezy wretches, you know, they are waiting for some one to do that to them. And I have to remind myself, I don't want to ruin my life.
So I mean I tell friends of mine that, young friends of mine, they call me about somebody and they go, bub, bub, bub, bub...... And I say, well
That's don't do them a favor. Don't do exactly what they expect you to do.

They are so masochistic underneath that surface sadism that they may have and grab and all that. I mean they are masochistic, they are really waiting for you to get them. It's like people waiting to get hit by cars, they can sue them. There are people around like that.

You don't want to get trapped like that, you know in an effort to get even with somebody. It's a tough lesson and when it happens you get by and you get red mad.

I'm waiting for a man to pay me some money now that I have coming to me from Capital. It's in a lawyer's office and that man's so mean that he stalls and stalls.

Yes. He'll give it to me. I said to him, I'll bet you I won't get that money until after New Year. He has to eventually. Already he's trying to eat it up by charging me another two hundred dollars for his office because they've had to go through some

so much trouble finding out their mistakes. These stories about what goes on in these music market places is so revolting that it's not really, it's better not to think about it. Once you know about it then you try to duck it, you know, you do what you can about it, but once you find out about it there's no use dwelling on it. You know, it's a question of style and everything, too...
(Unintelligible) The music market place is revolting.
